rejected.title: Water in the Asia region
card: Water shapes how people live in Asia. It affects what people grow, how they earn a living and what they believe.
Monsoon
a seasonal wind that brings heavy rain to much of South and South-East Asia. Many farmers depend on this rain to flood fields and grow rice, a main food crop.
Mekong River
a long river that flows through several countries in South-East Asia. Millions of people fish in it and its wetlands for food and income.
Ganges
a river that flows across northern India and is sacred to Hindus. People bathe in it and hold ceremonies on its banks, so its value is spiritual as well as practical.
rejected.remember: In Asia, water supports food, fishing and faith: monsoon rice, the Mekong's fish and the sacred Ganges.

a.q: Why do many rice farmers in South and South-East Asia depend on the monsoon?
opts: It brings heavy seasonal rain that waters their crops
It carries fish upstream into their rice fields
It makes the land cooler so rice can be stored
It melts snow that fills the rivers all year
a.why: The monsoon brings heavy rain in a particular season, and rice fields need plenty of water. The monsoon is a wind that brings rain, not a source of fish or snowmelt.
a.clue: Think about what rice fields need most.

b.q: Pham fishes on the Mekong River in Vietnam to feed his family and sell at market. Asha bathes in the Ganges in India as part of her faith. Which two parts of life do their uses show water shaping?
opts: How people earn a living and what they believe
What people grow and how they earn a living
What people grow and what they believe
How people travel and how they earn a living
b.why: Pham's fishing gives him food and income, so it is about earning a living. Asha's bathing in the Ganges is religious, so it is about what she believes. The tempting option pairs growing crops with belief, but Pham catches fish rather than growing anything.
b.clue: One person uses a river for work and the other for faith.
